First 10 minutes

Drop it into Gradle and wire one typed job.

Runtime model

Boundaries that survive contact with production.

Agents.KT focuses on the parts a framework can make deterministic: typed contracts, tool authorization, manifests, event streams, and deployment shapes that fit existing Kotlin services.

01

Compiler-checked contracts

`Agent<IN, OUT>` keeps responsibilities narrow. Purely typed composition fails at compile time when boundaries do not line up.

02

Least-privilege tools

Per-skill tool allowlists, typed handles, policy metadata, and before-interceptor hooks make access explicit and reviewable.

03

Audit evidence by construction

Permission manifests, JSONL exports, manifest hashes, and ledger verification turn runtime behavior into concrete review artifacts.

Composition DSL

Express the agent graph in the language your backend already speaks.

Sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out, forums, wrappers, loops, and typed routing are first-class operators instead of orchestration glue.

then

Release truth

A trust story with explicit non-goals.

The project is careful about the difference between in-runtime enforcement and deployer-owned controls. That honesty is the point: teams can review what the runtime owns and what still belongs to their gateway, OS sandbox, or compliance process.

Security model up front

Threat-model docs call out which boundaries are enforced and which are not.

Policy hooks before execution

Deny, mutate, or substitute skill turns and tool calls before work runs.

Manifest verification

CI can fail when capability boundaries widen unexpectedly.

Observable runtime

OTel, LangSmith, Langfuse, JSONL, and typed events share the same story.

Interop surfaces

One Kotlin runtime, multiple protocol doors.

Agents.KT can live inside an app, expose an agent as a server, or talk to external capabilities through protocol-native clients.

MCP Client, server, and standalone runner support.
A2A Server and typed client shape for agent-to-agent work.
AG-UI Streaming subset for lifecycle, text, reasoning, and tools.
NLWeb Partial /ask compatibility for single responses.
x402 Experimental seller and guardrails-first buyer flows.
AGNTCY OASF export/import, identity verify, and DIR clients.

Who should pick it

Use it when the agent layer belongs in Kotlin.

Agents.KT is strongest when the team already ships Spring, Ktor, Quarkus, or JVM services and wants the agent boundary to be code, not an external Python sidecar.

A

Backend teams

Keep agent orchestration inside the same language, build, and deployment model as the service.

B

Platform teams

Expose controlled agent capabilities through MCP without rewriting the runtime around the wire format.

C

Regulated builders

Produce manifests, runtime hashes, audit logs, and explicit policy decisions as review material.

Start with one typed boundary, then compose the graph.
